query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: LaH10 synthesized under extreme high-pressure conditions will exhibit superconductivity due to the formation of a dense hydrogen sublattice that enhances electron–phonon coupling.
generation.material_initial_state: Elemental lanthanum and molecular hydrogen at ambient conditions.
generation.intervention: Subject a lanthanum and hydrogen mixture to high-pressure (above 150 GPa) and high-temperature synthesis in a diamond anvil cell to form LaH10.
generation.conditions: High-pressure (>150 GPa) and high-temperature conditions in a controlled environment.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a cubic structure in LaH10, in which hydrogen atoms form a dense sublattice surrounding lanthanum.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced electron–phonon interactions mediated by high-frequency vibrational modes of hydrogen, leading to the formation of Cooper pairs required for superconductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A superconducting transition will be observed—with a critical temperature likely above 200 K—only under the high-pressure phase where LaH10 is stabilized.
generation.baseline: At ambient pressure where LaH10 cannot form, no superconductivity is expected.
generation.boundary: Superconductivity is confined to the high-pressure, cubic LaH10 phase; deviations in pressure or temperature may destabilize the phase and eliminate the superconducting state.
generation.uncertainty: While the general superconducting behavior is expected from LaH10, exact critical temperatures and the detailed pressure dependencies may vary due to synthesis reproducibility and sample inhomogeneities.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize LaH10 in a diamond anvil cell by subjecting a lanthanum-hydrogen mixture to pressures above 150 GPa and heat. Measure electrical resistance and magnetic susceptibility while cooling the sample from room temperature down to below 10 K.
measurements: Electrical resistance vs temperature (for detecting a superconducting drop to zero resistance)
Magnetic susceptibility measurements (for evidence of the Meissner effect)
X-ray diffraction (for confirming the formation of the cubic LaH10 phase)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant drop in resistance or no Meissner effect is observed in the high-pressure phase of LaH10, or if superconductivity occurs outside the high-pressure-induced phase, then the hypothesis is falsified.
